title: repository `find … ignoring <Cap>` / `ignoring *` — the capability-filter bypass on the ROW-shaped read path, crossed with a principal (`tenantOwned`) and a non-principal (`softDeletable`) filter, on a relational AND a `shape: document` aggregate
note: minted by M-T6.54 F18.  `projection-agg-filters` witnesses `ignoring` on a query-time PROJECTION and the tenancy fixtures witness the filters with no bypass anywhere, so `find … ignoring` over a PRINCIPAL filter had no fixture at all — and java kept the tenant conjunct on both of its read surfaces (relational @Query JPQL and the document `findAll()`) while the (since-deleted) `ignoring` backend gate's family list certified it as honouring the clause.  Every assertion over it is paired presence + ABSENCE: the failure mode is a RETAINED conjunct, invisible to a presence-only check.  Also pins the fail-OPEN direction — the root `findAll`/by-id reads carry no `ignoring` clause, so no OTHER find's bypass may widen them.  Since F-005 this fixture is also the corpus' only source of `loom.tenancy-filter-bypass` — four warnings, one per `ignoring`-bearing find over a `tenantOwned` aggregate, all TRUE positives (that crossing is the fixture's subject), and the only trips a full-corpus `ddd parse` sweep reports for that code.

authzGate.//: Widened reads (`find(C) ignoring …`) on both persistence shapes.  The ladder reads every seeded row back as a FOREIGN tenant — 404 on the by-id read, ABSENT from the collection, PRESENT under the bypassing reads — so these surfaces' refusals are tenant-scoped, which only a second tenant can observe.

elixir.//: The document-shape create demands the defaulted capability field, so no `Note` could be written; the capability table refuses the pair on elixir (`persistence:document` with `capability:softDeletable`) until it can.
elixir.reason: an author-declared create on a `shape: document` + `softDeletable` aggregate answers 422 `Required /data/isDeleted`, so the pair is refused on elixir

authzLadder.//: The TENANT half of `find … ignoring` on both persistence shapes: `acme` seeds a row and tenant `globex` reads it back.  Every clause-less read hides it (404 by id and by find; ABSENT from the 2xx collection), and the two bypassing finds return it — the control that proves the absent arms can fail.  The not-deleted half needs one tenant and is the case's own `test e2e` block.
